project: Bellwood Hub — Mayor's AI Chief of Staff
tagline: Graph-augmented, entity-resolved institutional-memory platform over the Village of Bellwood's ~70,000 municipal emails — a queryable chief of staff, not just search.
headline: 🔴 An open door, closed — 2026-07-30 found the production MCP endpoint serving all 125,459 personal messages and draft_reply to unauthenticated callers (BUG-10, now 401). The same session re-framed the product: root-cause work proved the live corpus holds 1 bellwood-addressed message and 2 .gov out of 125,459 — so the live instance is RD's personal Chief of Staff and the mayor's build becomes a separate release (DEC-18). Shipped Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 with per-task profiles, the brief-led three-panel dashboard shared by mobile and desktop, and the calendar (31 events, conflict flags). Deployed 7d602de → bellwood-dev, /chief 200.

glance.d: Deployed 2026-07-30 (7d602de). Four commits: model upgrade + task profiles, calendar fix, dashboard rebuild, docs. Verified after deploy: /chief 200, /hub 200, MCP 401 without key and 200 with it, auth callback origin pinned.

BUG-10, critical. bellwood-dev.vercel.app/api/mcp answered unauthenticated requests with the full toolset over the real 125,459-message mailbox, including draft_reply. Confirmed by retrieving a genuine invoice with no credentials. Vercel env vars only apply on redeploy, so the fix stayed inert until the deploy — now 401 without the key.

FEAT-45. SDK 0.40.1 → 0.115.0. A naive model-string swap would have 400'd every agent run: Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 both reject temperature, which completeMeta() sent on every call, and both default thinking ON, which shares the max_tokens budget and would have truncated the structured digests. Per-model knobs now live in TASK_PROFILE so a future generation is a table edit. Verified live: Haiku 4.5 rejects output_config.effort; Opus 5 rejects xhigh/max effort with thinking disabled.

FEAT-46. Seven widgets became a brief plus what's coming up, urgent email, and waiting on you. Mobile (NeedsToKnowCard) and desktop (DashboardHub) had drifted into different products; both now render the same components from components/chief/dashboard/panels.tsx. The brief carries per-desk attribution, a Run now button, and the next scheduled pass.

FEAT-47 + BUG-9. Two independent causes had kept the mirror empty for a week: the ingest cron selected only status='active' accounts (the Gmail account sat at 'error' from an unrelated mail 404), and the Google Calendar API was disabled on the Cloud project. Conflict detection is a pure function with 7 checks; all-day events are excluded deliberately.
DEP-6, owner RD. AUTH_URL is now pinned so the redirect_uri stops varying by hostname, but the two callback URIs must still be registered on OAuth client 32902323271-bhekte5q27… before sign-in works.
ISS-11. gmail 404: Requested entity was not found. 462 messages behind. This is also what tripped the calendar ingest's status filter.

ISS-9. MAX_THREADS = 400 and WINDOW_DAYS = 45 in lib/triage/run.ts. The retired Priority Matrix reported '97% FYI' — 97% of the 400, shown as though it described the whole mailbox. The bulk-mail classifier (FYI_SENDER) already exists and costs nothing; it is simply starved of scope.

The Mayor's landing screen: a 'Good morning, Mayor Harvey' Chief-of-Staff briefing (what happened / new / important) + today's calendar + sign-to-approve agent drafts inline + inbox preview, on mobile + desktop. A new R4 Chief of Staff agent summarizes every other agent's output. Hybrid generation: deterministic baseline keyless, OpenAI-voiced persona when a key is present; persona (name/greeting/tone/instructions) is configurable in Admin → Chief of Staff. Next: the Morning Agent (configurable web-search query cards, Supabase-backed).

Runs on JSON fixtures derived from the 30k seed — no DB or API dependency for the screens (DEMO_MODE=1). The bulletproof path for a live mayor demo; Ask still calls OpenAI for synthesis, and email drill-down hits Postgres.
Deployed to Vercel (public) and running locally. / redirects to /chief. Desktop ChiefApp + a dedicated mobile UI (bottom nav) switch at 768px. Public URL: web-seven-tawny-20.vercel.app.
Postgres (poc.*) fully loaded with OpenAI embeddings. Powers the click-through-to-source-email drill-down and the optional live semantic path (flip DEMO_MODE=0).
86,744 address · 43,370 person · 19,052 phone · 1,943 business rows across the corpus — the basis for the History (entity timeline) screen.

Project wwqebbqbnetkjibqmhlj (us-west-2, PG17). 19 tables across poc / canonical / pipeline / app schemas. Isolated from other projects for client-data separation; connects via the IPv4 session pooler.

Verified against the CTO brief: AD-1 ingestion decoupled from capability, AD-2 one Postgres / three access patterns, AD-3 resolved-conversation unit, AD-4 topics + RRF planner, AD-5 event-sourced issues, AD-6 assertion-ledger identity.

Captures inbox + recovered/deleted items toward the ~70k corpus. Needs Azure app registration + admin consent. Concrete version of product task #3. Outlook is also the source for the Calendar (TASK-11).

rows.t: TASK-10 · Security audit before going live
rows.detail: Full pre-production security audit / penetration test before any real mailbox data goes live — a go-live gate. Scope: adversarial threat model (brief §9 — a sitting official's email: FOIA, opposition research, breach exposure); enforce row-level RBAC via Postgres RLS (currently stubbed — ISS-4); PII detection + tagging at ingestion; encryption in transit + at rest; least-privilege DB roles per pipeline stage; secrets management + key rotation (RSK-1 / TASK-7); the immutable audit trail (ISS-5); NIST 800-53 + CJIS §5.4 control review for the police CJI data; dependency/SCA scan; auth review. Engage municipal counsel on FOIA / Open Meetings / records-retention. Pairs with ISS-5 (audit) and ISS-4 (RLS) — all post-demo.

issues.title: The MCP shared-secret guard fails OPEN when unset
issues.detail: app/api/[transport]/route.ts:181 reads `if (!secret) return true;` — any environment without MCP_SECRET serves the entire corpus and draft_reply to anonymous callers. MCP_SECRET was set on bellwood-dev and verified (401 without key), but bellwood-hub and bellwood-mayor were both answering 200 unauthenticated and were not fixed; local dev has no secret either. Fix: invert to fail closed, then set the secret per environment. Found by the RSK-7 adversarial audit.

issues.title: Several GET handlers write — a non-GET gate is not a read-only gate
issues.detail: GET /api/triage/senders seeds app.important_senders on first read (product state, not a cache). /api/wall, /api/queue, /api/inbox, /api/email and /api/agents/run each write an app.audit_log row per GET, and the middleware POSTs an access.page row per page view. Next 14 also auto-implements HEAD by invoking the GET handler verbatim, so HEAD is not inert. Blocking a viewer's non-GET requests therefore still leaves writes reachable.

issues.title: Production MCP endpoint served the entire personal mailbox unauthenticated
issues.detail: bellwood-dev.vercel.app/api/mcp answered any unauthenticated POST with the full five-tool set over canonical.messages (125,459 real messages) plus draft_reply. Confirmed by retrieving a genuine Zoom past-due invoice with no credentials. MCP_SECRET was set hours earlier but Vercel only applies env vars on redeploy, so the endpoint stayed open until the deploy. Verified after: 401 without the key, 200 with it.

issues.title: Calendar ingest was a silent no-op for a week
issues.detail: cron/ingest-calendar selected only status='active' accounts. The Gmail account sat at status='error' from an unrelated mail-sync 404, so the every-2-hours cron ran and did nothing. Calendar rides the Gmail grant but is a separate capability and must fail independently. Compounding second cause: the Google Calendar API was disabled on the Cloud project.

issues.title: OAuth redirect_uri_mismatch — AUTH_URL unset
issues.detail: NextAuth v5 derived the origin from whichever hostname was hit, so per-deployment URLs sent a redirect_uri that can never be pre-registered. Pinned AUTH_URL to https://bellwood-dev.vercel.app. Console URIs remain RD's action (DEP-6).

issues.title: Triage covers 400 of 125,459 messages (0.32%)
issues.detail: MAX_THREADS = 400 and WINDOW_DAYS = 45 in lib/triage/run.ts. The retired Priority Matrix showed '97% FYI' — 97% of that 400-thread sample, presented as the whole mailbox. The bulk-mail classifier already exists as the FYI_SENDER regex and buckets deterministically at zero model cost; the fix is scope, not a new classifier. Caution: Google security alerts and invoices are no-reply senders too, so the axis that matters is actionable-vs-ambient, not bulk-vs-personal.

issues.title: The privacy wall is not implemented in the live path
issues.detail: canonical.messages has no mailbox/lane column and retrieval applies no lane filter. mailbox_id is read in exactly three places, all to render a 'walled' label. Moving an account from gov to biz would change a badge and remove nothing from search. Low practical risk on a personal instance where everything is RD's own mail, but material for the mayor build where FOIA separation is a stated non-negotiable.

issues.detail: police, fire, council and constituent have each run 111 times and return the honest-empty sentinel every time. Only 3 of 9 desks invoke a model at all. Worth noting positively: they are honest — empty digests, no fabricated citations, exactly the R4 honest-gap behaviour, verified against real data.

issues.title: Ingest could stall a backfill permanently while reporting success
issues.detail: SELECT-then-INSERT against uq_raw_version. A provider batch can contain the same message twice (Gmail backfill, overlapping pages), so the second copy threw and unwound the whole 400-message round. The cursor only advances after a batch completes, so the next run re-pulled the same page — self-healing only because the duplicate was a race. A deterministic duplicate would loop forever, silently. Fixed: idempotent RAW landing plus per-message isolation; failures are now counted and reported rather than swallowed.

issues.title: app.audit_log was readable by the anon key
issues.detail: 004_audit.sql stopped at REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE — append-only is not private. The table is also absent from 003_rls.sql's array, whose schema-wide revoke ran before 004 created it. The ledger records who read which record plus IP/device/geo. MH-2 hit the same gap and fixed it by hand on the Mayor's DB; now encoded in the migration so it stops recurring on fresh projects.

issues.title: The Ask right rail fabricated metrics beside live answers
issues.detail: RetrievalPlan rendered a hardcoded '92%'; GapsPanel rendered hardcoded demo copy — '2 gaps in this answer', 'Public Works CSV at 78% coverage' — over live answers about a real mailbox. In a product whose promise is that it cites sources and states what is missing, a panel that invents missing things is the worst available bug. Deleted; replaced with the user's own recent searches. The honest no-records note was kept.

issues.title: constituent agent read 200 messages and reported nothing
issues.detail: 2026-07-18 live run: slice 200, digest 0. Either correct (a personal mailbox has no constituent business) or the uncited-point stripping in agent-runner.ts is too aggressive. Needs a look before the behaviour is trusted on the Mayor's mail.

issues.title: Abstract instructions retrieve noise
issues.detail: Measured on a real mailbox: 'invoices and payment requests' and 'meeting invitations' retrieved precisely; 'anything urgent that needs a reply from me' returned marketing copy. A top-score weak-match warning was built and removed — correct invoices (0.41) and pure junk (0.41) are indistinguishable by score. Mitigated by MIN_SCORE, the preview, and docs/AGENT_TEST_PLAN.md.

issues.title: No audit trail — must meet NIST 800-53 AU + CJIS §5.4 government auditing standards
issues.detail: ⏳ SCHEDULED POST-DEMO (RD, Jun 26) — deferred until after Monday; required before any real mailbox data. CRITICAL go-live blocker (not a demo blocker). STANDARDS: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 'AU' (Audit & Accountability) family is the federal baseline; CJIS Security Policy §5.4 applies because police blotter/incident data is Criminal Justice Information; add HIPAA §164.312(b) audit controls if fire/EMS PHI is indexed; retention per the Illinois Local Records Act. REQUIREMENTS — (1) LOG EVERY EVENT [AU-2/AU-12, CJIS 5.4.1.1]: searches/retrievals (/api/ask), record & document accesses (/api/email = CJI access), agent drafts, approvals/decisions, exports, logins (success+fail), permission and config changes. (2) RECORD CONTENT [AU-3, AU-8, CJIS 5.4.1.1.1]: synchronized timestamp, event type, system component, source (session/IP), actor identity, target (message_id/entity), outcome (success/fail), plus query text + result count. (3) PROTECTION [AU-9, AU-10]: append-only, tamper-evident (hash-chained), immutable — not modifiable or deletable by application roles; non-repudiation. (4) RETENTION [AU-11, CJIS]: at least 365 days, then per the local records schedule. (5) REVIEW & REPORTING [AU-6/AU-7, CJIS 5.4.3]: at-least-weekly review, searchable, exportable reports. IMPLEMENTATION: an append-only audit table + write-through middleware on every API action, written under a protected DB role, with a review/export surface.

Transparency is the trust mechanism.

decisions.text: The live instance is RD's personal Chief of Staff. Bellwood is the demo persona only; the mayor's version becomes a separate copy/release. Settled after root-cause work proved the corpus holds 1 bellwood-addressed message and 2 .gov out of 125,459 — the reported 'retrieval quality' problem was a missing municipal corpus, not a ranking failure.

Configuration stays with the developer. Agents, models and connectors are configured at the prompt/deploy level in Claude Code, not exposed as end-user settings — exposing them creates noise and confusion for the person the app is for. Motivates retiring most of AdminPanel (550 lines) and AgentsPage (879 lines).

Do not move the desks to Managed Agents. Each desk is a single structured completion — gather slice, one call, validate, store — not a tool loop, so there is no loop to hand over. Migrating would move citation validation, the audit ledger and the human send-gate off our infrastructure, and those three are the product. Instead add a tool-use loop over the five functions the MCP server already wraps.

One instruction box, not four fields. Configuring an agent meant charter + goals + urgency rules + focus — a taxonomy to learn before you could say what you wanted. Now one plain-English box; the old fields survive behind Advanced. The retrieval query is derived from the instruction by one Haiku call at save time, cached, and shown in the preview — never derived in the runner, because reading config must not cost a model call.

Route agents by meaning, not by enum. StreamKey is a closed 7-value union and the topics it switches on are never written on the live path, so live routing runs on sender-domain matching alone. Focus makes an agent's scope a sentence resolved semantically. Proof: the Google Security agent has no StreamKey at all and its first live run produced 4 cited findings. This is the mechanism the per-department fleet should be built on — one sentence per desk, not one enum value + regex + deploy each.

Ask runs on the canonical store; poc is dead. RETRIEVAL_BACKEND defaulted to poc, which is empty on any canonical-built stack, so a fresh instance silently answers '0 sources' and blames a missing OpenAI key. Flipped to canonical. Side effect: Ask no longer needs OpenAI at all — OpenAI now serves only Whisper voice, a narrower compliance entry (query audio, never record content).

North Star: ONE place for the Mayor to look, search, and build his day. The Chief of Staff organizes his inbox, confirms his calendar (agent-supported), powers AI Search, and builds summaries by area. Unifying concept: configurable Area views — e.g., Firehouse (contacts · events · tasks), Police (emails · notices · tasks), Public Works — each a single domain workspace, built up over time (FEAT-3).
Direction: this becomes an agent that connects to other agents (agent-to-agent / MCP) — the capability agents + MCP server are the foundation.

Jobs-to-be-done IA: mobile reorganized around tasks — Emails (queued-to-go + needs-attention), Events (was Commitments), Search, History (was Memory), Source. Renamed throughout; kept "institutional memory" as the brand tagline. Every email is clickable to the full source document.
Kept the JSON demo as the default (DEMO_MODE=1) over the live DB — reliability for the mayor demo.
Connect via the Supabase Session Pooler (IPv4) instead of the direct IPv6 host — no IPv4 add-on needed.
Fixed a latent migration bug (canonical message_topics excluded from the RLS loop — no tenant_id column) so the schema applies cleanly on a fresh DB.
